raw_text:
Below is a focused 3-week powerlifting peaking block designed to taper volume, maintain or slightly increase intensity, sharpen specificity, and ensure she’s fresh for meet day. Assumes her last accumulation/strength blocks are complete, technique is solid, and openers/attempt strategy will be set by end of Week 2. Full gym access. No injuries.

Guiding principles
- Specificity: Competition squat, bench, and deadlift as primaries with comp standards (pauses, commands in practice).
- Volume down, intensity maintained: Fewer hard sets, singles at or near top-set intensity with back-off work early, tapering further each week.
- Fatigue reduction: Drop accessory volume and lower RPE over weeks 1→3.
- Skill sharpening: Singles at 85–93% in Wk1–2; Wk3 is a short taper with light technique, mobility, and rest.
- Manage fatigue with low deadlift frequency in week of meet and spacing heavy exposures.

Estimated 1RM placeholders
- Use her current estimated 1RMs from end of accumulation/last heavy exposures. If unknown, anchor by RPE.
- Notation: % is of current e1RM; RPE for singles/back-offs to regulate.

Weekly overview
- Week 1 (21–15 days out): Peak strength signal, moderate taper in volume. Heavy singles 87–92% with controlled back-offs.
- Week 2 (14–8 days out): Final heavy exposures and opener confirmation. One near-second-attempt single on each lift (90–95%) early in week, then taper volume hard.
- Week 3 (Meet week, 7–0 days out): Deload/taper. Only light-to-moderate technique work early, full rest 48 hours before meet.

Week 1: 21–15 days out
Goal: Expose to near-max singles without accumulating fatigue. Maintain bar speed and confidence.

Day 1 – Squat focus
- Comp Back Squat
  - Work up to 1@88–90% e1RM, RPE 7.5–8
  - Back-off: 2–3 sets x 2 reps @ 80–82%, RPE 6–7
- Paused Squat (2-count)
  - 2 sets x 2–3 reps @ ~70–72%, RPE 6
- Accessories (reduced volume)
  - Hamstring hinge (RDL or back extension): 2 x 6–8, RPE 6
  - Light core (plank or side plank): 2 x 30–45s

Day 2 – Bench focus
- Comp Bench (pause, commands)
  - Work up to 1@88–90% e1RM, RPE 7.5–8
  - Back-off: 3 x 2 @ 80–82%, RPE 6–7
- Spoto or 1ct Paused Bench
  - 2 x 3 @ 72–75%, RPE 6
- Upper back: Chest-supported row 2 x 8, RPE 6
- Triceps: Pushdowns 2 x 10–12, RPE 6

Day 3 – Deadlift focus
- Comp Deadlift (her preferred stance)
  - Work up to 1@88–90% e1RM, RPE 7.5–8
  - Back-off: 2 x 2 @ 80–82%, RPE 6–7
- Deadlift variation (pause at mid-shin or tempo down)
  - 2 x 2–3 @ 70–72%, RPE 6
- Bracing/core: 2 x 8–10 (Pallof press or dead bug)

Day 4 – Secondary bench + light squat skill
- Comp Bench
  - Work up to 1@85–87%, RPE ~7.5
  - Back-off: 2 x 2 @ 78–80%, RPE 6–7
- Close-grip Bench
  - 2 x 3–4 @ 72–75%, RPE 6
- Light Squat (technique, speed)
  - 3 x 3 @ 65–70%, RPE 5–6
- Scap/rotator cuff: 2 x 12–15 easy

Notes for Week 1
- Total hard sets per lift reduced 25–35% from accumulation.
- Keep reps crisp; cut a set if bar speed slows. Sleep 7.5–9h.
- Nutrition: Maintenance to slight surplus (+100–200 kcal), 1.6–2.2 g/kg protein, sodium adequate, carbs centered pre/post sessions.

Week 2: 14–8 days out
Goal: Final heavy exposures, confirm openers, then taper volume aggressively.

Day 1 – Squat (heavy single) + light bench
- Comp Back Squat
  - Work up to 1@90–93% e1RM, RPE 8–8.5 (aim for likely opener+feel of 2nd)
  - Back-off: 1–2 x 1–2 @ 78–80%, RPE 6
- Light Bench (technique)
  - 3 x 3 @ 70–72%, RPE 6
- Minimal accessories: 1–2 easy sets core

Day 2 – Bench (heavy single)
- Comp Bench
  - Work up to 1@90–92% e1RM, RPE 8–8.5
  - Back-off: 2 x 1–2 @ 78–80%, RPE 6
- Optional: Very light upper back 2 x 8, RPE 5–6

Day 3 – Deadlift (heavy single)
- Comp Deadlift
  - Work up to 1@90–93% e1RM, RPE 8–8.5
  - Back-off: 1–2 x 1–2 @ 75–78%, RPE 6
- No accessory hamstring work beyond light mobility

Day 4 – Secondary bench, very light squat
- Comp Bench
  - Work up to 1@85–88%, RPE 7.5–8
  - Back-off: 1–2 x 2 @ 75–78%, RPE 6
- Light Squat
  - 2 x 2–3 @ 60–65%, RPE 5–6
- Shoulder prehab: 2 x 12–15 easy

Attempt planning at end of Week 2
- Determine openers based on Week 2 singles:
  - Opener: ~88–92% of true 1RM, or the best weight she can confidently triple on a great day; should move like RPE 6.5–7.
  - Second: ~95–98% based on opener speed and meet day feel.
  - Third: 100–103% if warranted by second attempt speed and confidence.
- Lock in commands practice each bench session. Review meet-day timing, warm-up flow, and equipment checks.

Nutrition/hydration for Week 2
- Maintain bodyweight. Keep carbs high around heavy single days.
- Sodium and fluids consistent. Fiber moderate; avoid new foods.

Week 3: Meet week (7–0 days out)
Goal: Shed fatigue, keep neural readiness, arrive fresh. No deadlifting after early week. Last exposures are light and fast.

Day 1 (Mon or 5–6 days out) – Squat + Bench (last meaningful touches)
- Comp Back Squat
  - Work up to 1@80–82%, RPE ~6.5–7
  - Back-off: 1–2 x 1–2 @ 70–72%, RPE 6
- Comp Bench
  - Work up to 1@80–82%, RPE ~6.5–7
  - Back-off: 1–2 x 1–2 @ 70–72%, RPE 6
- Very light mobility, no accessories

Day 2 (Tue/Wed or 4–5 days out) – Deadlift (last touch) + light bench
- Comp Deadlift
  - Work up to 1@75–80%, RPE 6–7
  - No back-offs
- Optional: Bench technique 2 x 2 @ 70%, RPE 6

Day 3 (Wed/Thu or 3–4 days out) – Bench only (speed/commands)
- Comp Bench
  - 3–4 singles @ 75–80% with full pauses/commands, RPE 6–6.5
- Light shoulder mobility; stop if any fatigue appears

Day 4 (Thu/Fri or 2–3 days out) – Very light full-body primer (optional)
- Squat: 2 x 1–2 @ 60–65%, RPE 5
- Bench: 2 x 1–2 @ 60–65%, RPE 5
- No deadlift
- If she prefers more rest, skip this day. Priority is freshness.

Day 5–6 (48 hours pre-meet onward)
- Rest, easy walking/mobility only. No lifting.
- Visualization, commands rehearsal, meet logistics.

Meet-day warm-up plan
- Timing: Start ~60–70 min before flight start. Last warm-up ~5–7 min before first attempt.
- Squat warm-ups (example for 150 kg opener; scale accordingly):
  - Bar x 5–10
  - 40% x 3
  - 55% x 2
  - 65% x 1–2
  - 75% x 1
  - 85–88% x 1 (last warm-up)
- Bench warm-ups similar progression to an 85–88% last single.
- Deadlift warm-ups start later and with fewer total reps:
  - Bar/empty just to groove
  - 40% x 2
  - 55% x 1
  - 70% x 1
  - 80–85% x 1 (last warm-up)

Recovery and readiness
- Sleep: 8–9 h nightly, consistent wake times. Naps 20–30 min if needed, not after 3 pm.
- Mobility: Short daily sequence (hips, T-spine, shoulders, ankles) 8–10 min, pain-free only.
- Stress: Keep non-training stress low; plan travel, equipment check, rack heights in advance.

Nutrition and hydration
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day.
- Carbs: High on training days in Weeks 1–2; in Week 3 maintain moderate-high but simplify food choices to reduce GI risk.
- Sodium/fluids: Keep consistent. If weigh-ins are same-day, avoid aggressive cuts; if 24-hr, plan any cut well in advance (not recommended this close unless routine).
- Pre-lift fueling: 2–3 h pre big sessions/meet: 1–2 g/kg carbs, familiar low-fiber foods; 20–40 g protein. Sips of sports drink and small carb snacks between attempts as tolerated.
- Caffeine: Use normal dose on meet day; avoid novel high doses.

Load and RPE guardrails
- If any single exceeds RPE 8.5 in Week 1–2, reduce planned top set by 2–3% and/or trim back-offs.
- Bar speed slower than expected: prioritize technique, cut volume, keep confidence high.
- No grinders in Week 2–3.

Optional adjustments based on her tendencies
- Fast fatiguer: Drop one back-off set in Week 1 and all back-offs in Week 2 after top singles.
- Deadlift recovery-limited: Move Week 2 deadlift heavy single earlier (e.g., Day 1 or 2) and add an extra rest day before squats if needed.
- Bench frequency responder: Keep the light bench touches in Week 3; for non-responders, reduce to one touch only.

Outcome targets
- Arrive with low soreness, high bar speed, and rehearsed commands.
- Openers that are certain makes, second attempts to secure PR territory without risk, thirds for stretch goals if warranted.

This structure tapers total work each week while preserving heavy singles and specificity so she’s sharp and fresh on meet day.
